title: Present & Future Tenses: The Complete Picture
grammarTitle: Present & Future Tenses — Choosing with Precision
grammarNote: На B1 уровне ключевой навык — не просто знать каждое время, а понимать тонкие различия между похожими временами. Настоящее Простое vs Непрерывное, Настоящее Совершенное Simple vs Continuous, три способа выразить будущее — всё это требует понимания смысла, а не просто правил.

grammarTable.subject: Present Simple
grammarTable.example: "She studies every day." / "Water boils at 100°C." / "The course starts in September."

grammarTable.subject: Present Continuous
grammarTable.example: "She's studying now." / "He's living in Uralsk this year." / "I'm meeting her tomorrow."

grammarTable.subject: Present Perfect Simple
grammarTable.example: "She has finished the essay." / "He's never been to Almaty." / "They've just arrived."

grammarTable.subject: Present Perfect Cont.
grammarTable.example: "She's been studying for two hours." / "It's been raining since morning."

grammarTable.subject: going to
grammarTable.example: "I'm going to apply." (plan) / "Look — it's going to rain!" (evidence)

grammarExtra.title: Present Simple vs Present Continuous: state vs moment

rows.example: "She works at the library." (general truth) / "He doesn't eat meat." (habit) ✅
"She's working at the library this month." (temporary) / "He's not eating much lately." (recent pattern) ✅
"I know her." / "She wants to leave." / "He understands perfectly." ✅ NOT "I'm knowing her." ✗
"I'm meeting the professor tomorrow at 3." (confirmed arrangement with time) ✅

grammarExtra.title: Present Perfect Simple vs Continuous: result vs process

rows.example: "She has finished the report." (done — result) / "Have you ever been to Istanbul?" (experience) ✅
"She has been writing the report." (still writing, or just stopped — process matters) ✅

rows.form: PPC with FOR/SINCE (duration up to now)
rows.example: "He's been studying English for 10 years." / "She's been working here since 2022." ✅
"She has written 3 essays this week." (count) NOT "has been writing 3 essays" ✗

grammarExtra.title: Three future forms: will / going to / Present Continuous

rows.example: "I'll get that for you." (just decided) / "It will be difficult." (prediction) ✅

rows.form: going to = pre-made plan or evidence
rows.example: "I'm going to apply for the scholarship." (already decided) / "Look — it's going to rain!" ✅
"I'm flying to Almaty on Friday." (ticket booked, specific time) ✅
"The train leaves at 7 p.m." / "The exam starts at 9 a.m." (timetable) ✅
✅ "I've known her for years." — stative verbs → PPS not Continuous!

rows.form: "I'm going to meet her tomorrow at 3." ✗ (if booked)
rows.example: ✅ "I'm meeting her tomorrow at 3." — confirmed arrangement = PC ✅
✅ "She's written 3 essays." — counting = PPS. Continuous cannot count. ✅

rows.form: "I will go to Almaty next week." ✗ (if ticket bought)
rows.example: ✅ "I'm going to Almaty next week." — pre-arranged plan = going to or PC ✅

grammarTip:
Present & Future — точность выбора на B1:

PS vs PC:
→ Факт/привычка → Simple: "She works here."
→ Сейчас/временно → Continuous: "She's working here this month."
→ Stative глаголы (know/want/like) → ТОЛЬКО Simple!

PPS vs PPC:
→ Результат завершён → Simple: "She has finished."
→ Процесс/продолжительность → Continuous: "She's been working for hours."
→ Считаем (3 times/5 books) → ТОЛЬКО Simple!

Will vs Going to vs PC:
→ Спонтанно → will: "I'll help you."
→ Запланировано заранее → going to: "I'm going to apply."
→ Договорено + конкретное время → PC: "I'm meeting her at 3."
→ Расписание → PS: "The train leaves at 7."

exercises.instruction: PS or PC? Choose the correct form.
exercises.text: "This year, Amir ___ a timetable app for WKU students." (temporary project)
exercises.hint: Temporary ongoing project = Present Continuous. "This year, Amir IS BUILDING a timetable app." ✅

exercises.text: "She ___ the whole chapter already. You can borrow the book." (completed, result)
exercises.hint: Completed — result available now = Present Perfect SIMPLE. "She HAS READ the chapter." ✅

exercises.text: "I ___ (study) English for ten years, and I'm still learning."
exercises.hint: Duration up to now = PPC. "I HAVE BEEN STUDYING English for ten years." ✅

exercises.text: Rustam sees Kamila struggling with her bags. He says: "___ help you with those."
exercises.hint: Spontaneous decision at the moment of speaking = WILL. "I'LL help you." ✅

exercises.text: "I ___ Daniyar for coffee on Saturday. We arranged it last week."
exercises.hint: Confirmed arrangement with specific time = Present Continuous. "I'M MEETING Daniyar on Saturday." ✅
"understand" = stative verb → always Present Simple! "I UNDERSTAND what you mean." ✅ Never "I am understanding." ✗
Counting completed achievements = PPS. "She HAS WRITTEN five essays." ✅ NOT "has been writing five essays." ✗
Visible evidence → prediction = GOING TO. "It'S GOING TO rain!" ✅ (You can see the evidence.)

exercises.text: "The university café ___ at 8 a.m. every day." (fixed schedule)
exercises.hint: Fixed daily schedule = Present Simple. "The café OPENS at 8 a.m." ✅

exercises.text: "She usually ___ in the library, but this month she ___ from home."
exercises.hint: General habit = PS. Temporary this month = PC. "She usually STUDIES... but this month she IS WORKING from home." ✅

exercises.text: "I'm going to meet her tomorrow at 3" is always wrong — it should be "I'm meeting."
opts: False — both "going to" and PC can work; PC emphasises the confirmed time
exercises.correct: False — both "going to" and PC can work; PC emphasises the confirmed time
exercises.hint: Both "going to" (pre-made plan) and PC (confirmed arrangement) work here. PC is more natural when there's a specific time. ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the best sentence in context.
exercises.text: "She's in the exam right now. By the time she comes out, we ___ for two hours."
exercises.hint: A duration completed by a future moment = Future Perfect. "We WILL HAVE WAITED for two hours." ✅ (B1 preview — Future Perfect)

questions.hint: Present Simple = facts, habits, routines, general truths, official schedules. ✅

opts: Something happening now or temporarily + confirmed arrangements
questions.correct: Something happening now or temporarily + confirmed arrangements
questions.hint: PC = happening now, temporary situations, and confirmed future arrangements. ✅
PPS = completion/result ("has finished"), life experience ("has visited"), recent news ("has just arrived"). ✅
PPC = how long something has been going on ("has been studying for 2 years"). ✅

questions.text: "___ (know) her for ten years." (stative verb + duration)
questions.hint: "know" = stative → PPS only. "I HAVE KNOWN her for ten years." ✅ NEVER "have been knowing." ✗

questions.text: "She's been writing 5 essays this semester." — What is wrong?
opts: "has been writing" cannot be used with counting — should be "has written"
questions.correct: "has been writing" cannot be used with counting — should be "has written"
questions.hint: ✅ "She HAS WRITTEN 5 essays." — counting = PPS. Continuous cannot count. ✅

opts: A spontaneous decision or simple future
questions.correct: A spontaneous decision or simple future
questions.hint: "will" = spontaneous offer/decision OR general prediction. "I'll call you" = not pre-planned. ✅

questions.text: "I'm flying to Almaty on Friday." (PC for future) — appropriate because:
opts: The arrangement is confirmed with a specific time
questions.correct: The arrangement is confirmed with a specific time
questions.hint: PC for future = confirmed arrangement with specific time. ✅

questions.text: "Look at those clouds — it's going to rain." — "going to" because:
questions.hint: Going to + evidence: you can SEE the clouds = evidence-based prediction. ✅

questions.text: "The train ___ at 7:15. Don't be late." (fixed timetable)
questions.hint: Fixed transport schedule = Present Simple. "The train LEAVES at 7:15." ✅

questions.text: "She ___ here for 3 years and she loves it." (duration, still working)
questions.hint: Duration up to now + still ongoing → PPC. "She HAS BEEN WORKING here for 3 years." ✅

questions.text: Which sentence shows CORRECT use of all tenses?
questions.hint: "know" = stative → PPS. "has KNOWN him SINCE 2020." ✅ (NOT "has been knowing" — stative can't be continuous!)
